SIND TEXTBOOK BOARD EMLOYEES (EFPICIENCY
SIND TEXTBOOK BOARD EMPLOYEES
(EFFICIENCY AND DISCIPLINE) RULES, 1977
[Gazette of Sind,
Extraordinary, Part IV‑A, 11th August 1977]
No. S. O. (S&B) BSE‑361/76.‑In
exercise of the powers conferred by section 2 of the Textbook Hoard Ordinance,
1970 (Sind Ordinance No. XII of 1970) and after having received the approval of
Government, the Government of Sind are pleased to make the following rules :‑----
1. Short title, application, and commencement.‑(I) These rules may be called the Sind Textbook
Board Employees (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1977.
(2) They shall come into force
at once.
2. Definitions.‑In these
rules unless the context requires otherwise ;‑
(a) "accused" means an employee against
whom action is taken under these rules.
(b) "Authority" means the appointing
authority;
(c) "authorized officer" means an officer
of the Board authorised by the authority to perform functions of an authorized
officer under these rules ;
Provided that the Authorized Officer shall be at
least one grade above rte accused ;
(d) "Board" means the
Sind Textbook Board;
(e) "employee" means
an employee of the Board;
(j) "major penalty" means any penalty
specified in clause (b) of sub‑rule
(1) of rule 4;
(g) "minor penalty'' means any penalty specified
in clause (a) of sub. rule (1) of rule 4;
(h) "misconduct" means conduct prejudicial
to good order of service discipline
or contrary to rules relating to conduct of the Board's employee or unbecoming
of an Officer and a gentleman and includes any act on the part of an employee
to bring or attempt to bring political or other outside influence directly or
indirectly to bear on the members or officers of the Board in respect of any
matter relating to the appointment, promotion transfer, punishment, retirement
or other conditions of service of an employee; and
(i) "penalty" means a penalty which may be
imposed under theca rules.
3. Grounds of
penalty.‑Any one or mare penalties may be imposed on an employee if
he‑
(a) is inefficient, or has ceased to be efficient;
whether by reason of infirmity of mind or bossy, or otherwise, and is not
likely to recover his efficiency; or
(b) is guilty of misconduct; or
(c) is corrupt, or may
reasonably be considered corrupt because‑‑
(i) he, or any of his dependents or any other person
through him, or on his behalf, is in possession (for which he cannot reasonably
account) of pecuniary‑ resources or of property disproportionate to his
known sources of income; or
(ii) he has assumed a style of
living beyond his ostensible means; of
(iii) he has a persistent
reputation of being corrupt.
(d) is engaged, or is reasonably suspected of being
engaged in subversive activities, or is reasonably suspected of being
associated with others engaged in subversive activities, and whose retention in
service is, therefore, considered prejudicial to national security.
4. Penalties.‑‑(I) The penalties which may be imposed
under these rules are as follows :‑??????????
(a) Minor Penalties
(i) Censure;
(ii) Withholding, for a specific period promotion or
increment. with or without cumulative effect including stoppage at an
efficiency bar for a specified period in.
the time scale, otherwise than for unfitness to cross such bar; and
(iii) recovery from his pay of the whole or part of
any pecuniary lose ?cause d to the Board by negligence or breach of orders.
(b) Major
Penalties;
(i) reduction to a lower post or time‑scale, or
to a lower stage in a time scale;
(ii) compulsory retirement;
(iii) removal from service, and
(iv) dismissal from service.
(2) Removal from service does not, but dismissal from
service does, disqualify for future employment.
(3) In this rule removal or dismissal from service
does not include the discharge of an employee‑

or in accor?dance with the rules relating to probation or training applicable
